ledger.claim: The baseline for this trip is the matched pooled itinerary, not the rider's solo distance. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL, so under POL-RD-12 the POL-RD-01 optimal is trip_record.optimal_distance_km of 19.40 km. The governing actual figure is the GPS trace: derived.deviation.trace_distance_km is 20.18 km, giving an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal (3.88 km) AND 0.8 km absolute. 0.78 km clears neither limb and misses the absolute limb by 20 metres. No deviation is established, and under POL-RD-01 the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The rider's 15.8 km figure is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km, carried on the record for reference only. Under POL-RD-12 a claim that measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. The 4.4 km shortfall the claim_text asserts (20.2 minus 15.8) is an artefact of that mis-citation, not of anything the driver did. Both figures are on EV-TRIP-00113 and the ruling should name them side by side so it is visible why the arithmetic changes.

The detour the rider complains of — 'the driver went off to Hougang' — is the matched co-rider pickup, and POL-RD-12 excludes it by name: distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation and is removed from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The trace shows the vehicle stationary at Hougang Central for the boarding stop, consistent with a pick-up rather than a wander.

The rider was on notice before the wheels turned, so this is not a case of a route being altered behind his back. The platform's own match notification MSG-00113-001, sent 18:42:04, states 'Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min'; the log records it read at 18:42:31, and the trip did not start until 18:47:10. The 19.4 km matched-itinerary figure on the trip record is the same figure the rider was quoted in the app.

The driver's counterparty statement is corroborated rather than contradicted by the platform's own records: he says a second passenger was matched at Hougang and that he drove the app route, and the system notification MSG-00113-001 records that match, MSG-00113-003 records his contemporaneous explanation 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route', and the trace shows the stop. Nothing in the admitted evidence shows the vehicle anywhere the matched pooled itinerary did not put it.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired trace. The trace here is unimpaired: 217 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 and a 10 s sampling interval — so there is no gap, jump or sampling defect under POL-RD-07. What that clean trace shows is 0.78 km and 4.02%. The threshold is not met, the burden never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause need be invoked to defeat the claim.

No driver_profile check is engaged on this trip. POL-RD-06 is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation, and a 0.78 km excess is far below the 8.0 km / 50% material gate. In any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 471, so there is no repeat-deviation pattern, no POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is justified.

No traffic advisory covers the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridors in this window — EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0 — and the driver does not need one. The exoneration relied on is POL-RD-12, the platform's own matched pooled-itinerary baseline, not POL-RD-03. No closure is asserted, so the absence of an advisory costs this defence nothing; it is cited only so the absence is on the record.

The fare breakdown is METERED on rate card RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDEPOOL, its line items reconcile, distance_charged_km of 20.2 matches the 20.18 km the trace records, erp_gantries is empty and airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and a 3.00 pool discount was applied in the rider's favour. Every dollar charged traces to a line the rider actually consumed.

The disputed charge still stands: fare_breakdown.payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The dispute is rider-filed, so NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 is party-relative and preserves that present state — on this record the $6.00 contested stays with the driver. The driver drove the pooled itinerary the platform matched for him and quoted to the rider; the evidence does not support a refund against him, and it should not be invented to produce one.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides ultimately agree on the arithmetic, and the records confirm it. This was a RYDE_POOL booking (TRP-00113, EV-TRIP-00113), so under POL-RD-12 the correct baseline is the matched pooled-itinerary distance of 19.40 km stored on the trip record at match time, not the 15.80 km solo figure. The app told you this before the wheels turned: at 18:42:04 the platform's own notification (MSG-00113-001, read 18:42:31) said 'Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min', and the trip did not start until 18:47:10. The 15.80 km in the filing is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km, carried for reference only, and a claim measured against it fails on that ground alone. The governing actual distance is the GPS trace, not the bill: EV-GPS-00113 (weight 1.0) is unimpaired — 217 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, 10-second cadence — and records trace_distance_km of 20.18 km. Excess is 20.18 − 19.40 = 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 20% (3.88 km) and 0.8 km absolute; 0.78 km fails both and misses the absolute limb by about 20 metres. No deviation is established and no refund runs. The Hougang stop is the platform-matched co-rider pickup, which POL-RD-12 excludes from excess by name; the driver drove the itinerary he was matched to and said so contemporaneously (MSG-00113-003). The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00113, weight 1.0, METERED on RC-SG-2026Q3-RYDEPOOL) shows no billing-integrity defect: it reconciles to the cent, the 20.2 km billed matches the 20.18 km trace, erp_gantries is empty, no airport surcharge applies, and a $3.00 pool discount was applied in your favour — nothing is refundable under POL-RD-09(4). Because there is no material deviation, no POL-RD-06 driver-profile check or conduct referral arises, and driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 471 completed trips in any event. This is a rider-filed dispute and the result is NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: the $6.00 contested stays with the driver and payment_status remains CHARGED. Your profile contention is noted and accepted as far as it goes — deviation_claims_60d of 1 is far below the POL-RD-08 threshold and no other profile field was used against you — but it does not change the outcome, which turns entirely on the trace and the matched-itinerary baseline. Confidence is high because nothing decides this case but clean, weight-1.0 instruments; the absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00113-01, weight 0.0) is relied on by neither side for the outcome.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
